span: if it is found that the subsequent FIR is an abuse of process of law and/or the same has been lodged only to harass the accused, the same can be quashed in exercise of powers under Article 226 of the Constitution or in exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
why: Court states that an FIR which is an abuse of process can be quashed under s.482.

span: The impugned judgments and orders passed by the High Court are set aside, and the respective FIRs/investigation/ criminal proceedings be proceeded against the respective accused
why: Headnote holding: the High Court's quashing of FIRs on the basis of compromise is set aside because relevant circumstances were not considered.

span: the High Court must bear in mind the parameters for the exercise of the jurisdiction for quashing
why: About reasons needed for an interim stay of arrest while a quashing petition is pending, not the power to quash.

span: Section 482 of Cr.P.C. saves the inherent power of the High Court to make orders necessary to secure the ends of justice.
why: Headnote holding that s.482 empowers the High Court to examine whether the complaint's averments disclose an offence; the appeal is allowed and the complaint quashed (see preceding headnote text).

span: it could quash a first information report
why: Quoted Kurukshetra University remark expressing surprise that a High Court quashed an FIR before investigation began; the next paragraph adopts the principle of sparing use but this passage is the quotation.

span: This was a fit case for the High Court to exercise its inherent power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR.
why: Court holds the High Court erred in refusing and that this was a case for quashing the FIR under s.482.
